headline: Sequence models gain MPRA supervision, 3D context and single-molecule chromatin for variant effects
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Prediction
summary: Preprints extend sequence-to-function variant scoring with MPRA fine-tuning, single-molecule accessibility and 3D genome inputs, alongside multiomic variant-to-gene atlases.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting regulatory consequences of noncoding variants from sequence and functional genomic context. Sequence-to-function models are being refined: Borzoi is fine-tuned on synthetic MPRA variant-effect labels, raising CAGI5 and eQTL correlations, while eQIF aggregates Enformer predictions into an unsupervised per-variant score. A second strand moves to single-molecule resolution: ChAI-Net, S2d/Mola and FiberBrowser model or infer per-molecule chromatin states and co-accessibility. CellReg3D adds Hi-C 3D context to DNA language model embeddings. Published work covers a methylation compendium with the Wreath model, the mV2G tissue-specific variant-to-gene atlas, and XGBoost-SHAP prioritization of variants affecting HNF4A motifs. New elements are MPRA-based supervision, 3D context and single-molecule chromatin targets.
